subject: Hosted inference canary: throughput + p95/p99 spike impacting Hyperion prod
messages:
From: Alex Soto <alex.soto@hyperionhealth.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, support@hyperionhealth.com
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 09:14:02 -0700
Subject: [URGENT] Hosted inference canary causing prod latency & error increase

Hi Jonas,

We just noticed a sharp jump in p95/p99 and a small uptick in 5xx errors starting at ~08:45 PDT after the canary you pushed for model v2. Compared to the previous hour: p95 went from ~220ms to ~1.1s, p99 jumped to ~2.4s, and error rate climbed from 0.02% to 0.9%. Traffic is still within normal volume for our tier.

This is impacting our user-facing inference latency for the Chat endpoint. Can you triage immediately? We attached the runbook we used when this started. We can hop on a call — ops team is available now.

Thanks,
Alex Soto
SRE, Hyperion Health
[attachment: runbook-hostedapi.pdf]
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Alex Soto <alex.soto@hyperionhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 09:20:30 -07:00
Subject: Re: [URGENT] Hosted inference canary causing prod latency & error increase

Thanks Alex — we see the alert in our console as well (p95/p99 visible). Looping in Marcus (SRE lead) and Marissa (CS) to coordinate. Short plan: 1) pause/stop canary traffic to v2, 2) roll traffic back to v1 and enable fallback policy, 3) collect diagnostic traces and heap/KV stats.

Marcus — can you confirm we can cut canary traffic now and whether a fast rollback will trigger cold-start penalties? Grace — can you prep an update to Hyperion execs and confirm they want a partial credit offer? I'll set up a 30-min bridge.

--
Jonas Weber
Eng, Redwood Inference

Alex — thanks for flagging. Apologies for the disruption; we take these seriously. We agree with pausing the canary immediately. Jonas — please go ahead and cut v2 traffic.

I'll draft a succinct customer-facing note for Hyperion execs and copy Ben (sales lead) to discuss credits/contractary impact. Suggested wording: short apology, rollback confirmation, ETA for root cause analysis and 72-hour postmortem.

Can Hyperion share any request traces (with ids) where you saw the highest p99s? That will help correlate traces to model behavior.

Best,
Marissa Cole

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: Alex Soto <alex.soto@hyperionhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 09:35:58 -07:00
Subject: Re: [URGENT] Hosted inference canary causing prod latency & error increase

Update from SRE side (quick, actionable):
- We've inspected the runtime metrics and KV-cache eviction counters for the canary instances. v2's attention cache profiles appear to cause significantly higher KV usage per request; memory churn spikes when sequence-length distribution hits ~1.5x normal. That correlates with queueing and increased p95/p99.
- Immediate mitigation: cut canary weight to 0% (pausing traffic to v2) and route all requests to v1. This is low-risk and reversible. Expect ~10-30s for in-flight drains; cold-start tail for some pods ~200-400ms.
- Next steps for engineering: capture a heap profile, collect the kv-eviction logs (I've started that), and run a controlled replay of the failing request ids in a staging cluster.

Commands I'm running now:
- rctl rollout set canary/model-v2 0
- rctl metrics export hyperion-prod/kv-eviction --last 30m > diag-kv-eviction.tar.gz

Attaching diag export when ready.

Marcus Lin
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
[attachment: diag-kv-eviction.tar.gz]

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 10:01:12 -07:00
Subject: Re: [URGENT] Hosted inference canary causing prod latency & error increase

Alex/Priya — we cut canary traffic to v2 to 0% at 09:38 PDT. Metrics show p95 trending back toward baseline; p99 improving but still noisy. Marcus collected the kv-eviction export and we're replaying 20 sample requests in staging to reproduce the path.

Action items and asks:
- Hyperion: please share 3-5 request ids with the heaviest tail so we can replay exact inputs.
- Marcus & Eng: prep a brief RCA draft (timeline, root cause hypothesis, mitigation, long-term fix) within 72 hours.
- Marissa & Ben: propose an outbound customer note + a one-time credit (we recommend 20-25% of last month's hosted usage for Hyperion while we investigate).

I've scheduled a 30-min sync at 10:15 PDT. I'm also pulling executive attention (Ben, if you can join briefly we may need approval for the proposed credit and any SLA flex).

Thanks everyone for the quick responses. We'll follow up with the postmortem and next steps.

Jonas Weber
Eng, Redwood Inference
